newsitem.title: USA: Washington Post endorses Bill Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Washington Post endorses Bill Clinton.

text.p: The Washington Post endorsed President Bill Clinton for re-election on Wednesday but said the "choice for president this year is pretty bleak."
In an editorial, the newspaper criticised both Democrat Clinton and his Republican challenger Bob Dole for abandoning their past positions in an "I'll-say-or-do-anything campaign."

The newspaper had enthusiastically endorsed Clinton in 1992 and it praised the president for his positions on Supreme Court nominations, gun control, environmental laws and the North American Free Trade Agrement.

"But on too many fundamental issues -- above all, by the standard of steadfastness -- his administration has been disappointing and deficient and sometimes tawdry," the newspaper said. "Who can be sure which Bill Clinton will be president, if, as generally expected, he wins a new term."

The Post said in the end it leaned toward Clinton because Dole had proven incapable of exploiting an opening for an opposition party. Dole "turns out...to have little or nothing to say to the American public."
"In sum, Mr. Clinton's shortcomings are more evident and inescapable than they were four years ago," the paper wrote.

"But somewhere in that changeable figure, we believe, lies a capacity to be better at the job of the presidency than he has been -- and his opponent has given the nation any reason to believe he would be. On that uncertain basis, we choose Bill Clinton over Bob Dole."
